## Sliding windows of IT

Multi-unit activations from IT recordings were averaged over different windows with the following parameters:

- `onset`: 60, 70, ..., 150 start after stimulus presentation, and
- `l`: 50, 100, or 150 ms windows.

(For convenience, I often report the time in terms of bin number, e.g., `l` of 50 ms is an `l` of 5 bins.)

### Split-half correlations

::: {.callout-note}
**Archived implementation.** The IT sliding-window split-half correlations were computed by `scripts/split_corrs_rgn_onset_l.R` and `scripts/split_corrs_it_sliding.sh` (with `R/split_half_corr.R`), all since removed. Known issues with that implementation: it used all 20 ordered combinations of `combn(6, 3)` (each 3-vs-3 partition counted twice), averaged correlations directly rather than in Fisher z-space, did not apply the Spearman-Brown correction, and handled blanks inconsistently across settings (one aggregated blank group for the median onset/150 ms values, blanks excluded elsewhere). The current script covers other onsets/windows by editing `config/split_corrs.yml`. They were replaced by `scripts/split_corrs.R` and `R/reliability.R`; corrected values for all regions, onsets, windows, and blank handling are in `data/processed/20261104/split_corrs.csv` (see notebooks/20261104). To inspect the exact code used here, run `git show a3c5039:<path>`, e.g., `git show a3c5039:scripts/split_corrs.R`.
:::

In general, split-half correlations tend to be higher with later onsets and longer windows (@fig-corr_dist). 

```{r}
params <- expand.grid(
  region = "IT",
  onset = 6:15, 
  l = 5 * 1:3)

avg_corr <- function(region, onset, l, data_dir = here(out_dir, "split_corrs")) {
  here(data_dir, paste0(region, "_", onset, "_", l, ".csv")) %>%
    read.csv() %>%
    apply(1, mean) %>%
    data.frame(corr = .) %>%
    mutate(
      site = row_number(), 
      region = region, 
      onset = onset, 
      l = l)
}

it_corrs <- lapply(
  1:nrow(params), 
  function(i) avg_corr(params[i, "region"], params[i, "onset"], params[i, "l"])) %>%
  do.call(rbind, .)
```


```{r}
#| label: fig-corr_dist
#| fig-cap: "Violin plots of the split-half correlations for sites in IT as a function of the start of the averaging window and separated by the length of the window in rows. Distributions tend to stabilize after certain start times, with the stabilization occurring earlier for longer windows."
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 4

it_corrs %>%
  mutate(onset = 10 * onset, l = paste0(10 * l, " ms window")) %>%
  mutate(onset = factor(onset), l = factor(l)) %>%
  mutate(l = relevel(l, ref = "50 ms window")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(onset, corr, fill = l)) + 
    geom_violin(trim = F, alpha = 0.5) + 
    geom_boxplot(width = 0.06, fill = "white") + 
    facet_grid(rows = vars(l), scales = "fixed") + 
    labs(
      x = "Start of window after stimulus presentation (ms)", 
      y = "Split-half correlation (Pearson's ρ)", 
      fill = NULL) + 
  theme(
    legend.position = "none", 
    panel.spacing = unit(1, "lines")) 

```

### Mahalanobis distances

Higher split-half correlations do not necessarily indicate a better window for the subsequent

```{r}
source(here("R", "dM.R"))

dM_window <- function(mua, onset, l, grps) {
  start_idx <- STIM_IDX + onset
  dat <- mua[, start_idx:(start_idx + l), ] %>% 
    apply(c(1, 3), mean)
  dM_pairwise(dat, grps, shrink = T, return_diff = F)
}
```

```{r}
it_mua <- here("data", "processed", "20260625", "IT.qs2") %>%
  qs_read()
stimuli <- here("data", "processed", "20260826", "stimuli.csv") %>%
  read.csv()

incl_idx <- (stimuli$coherence == 2) & (stimuli$family != 0)
it_mua <- it_mua[incl_idx, , ]
stimuli <- stimuli[incl_idx, ]

fam_grps <- stimuli$family
temp <- dM_window(it_mua, 5, 5, fam_grps)
```
